title: Picea omorika
wikitext: {{Short description|Species of conifer}} {{Speciesbox | name = Serbian spruce | image = Picea omorika, Zaovine, Serbia 1.jpg | image_caption = In its native range near [[Zaovine]], Serbia. Note the extremely slender crown. | status = EN | status_system = IUCN3.1 | status_ref = {{cite iucn |author=Aleksić, J.M. |author2=Ballian, D. |author3=Isajev, D. |author4=Mataruga, M. |author5=Christian, T. |author6=Gardner, M. |date=2017 |title=''Picea omorika'' |volume=2017 |article-number=e.T30313A84039544 |doi=10.2305/IUCN.UK.2017-2.RLTS.T30313A84039544.en |access-date=12 November 2021}} | genus = Picea | species = omorika | authority = ([[Josif Pančić|Pančić]]) [[Emanuel von Purkyne|Purk.]] | range_map = Picea omorika range.svg | range_map_caption = {{Color box|#70A800}} Continuous range '''✖''' Isolated population }} '''''Picea omorika''''', the '''Serbian spruce''' (in {{langx|sr|Панчићева оморика, Pančićeva omorika}}, {{IPA|sh|pâːnt͡ʃit͡ɕɛv̞a ɔmɔ̌rika|pron}}, "Pančić's spruce"),{{cite web | url = https://www.plantea.com.hr/panciceva-omorika/ | title = ''Pančićeva omorika''| author = Gligić, Vojin| author2 = Šilić, Čedomil| author3 = Vukičević, Emilija| name-list-style = amp| year = 2021| access-date = 2021-03-20}} is a [[species]] of [[Pinophyta|coniferous tree]] [[endemic (ecology)|endemic]] to the [[Drina]] River valley in western [[Serbia]], and eastern [[Bosnia and Herzegovina]], with a total range of only about 60 [[hectare|ha]], at {{convert|800-1600|m|ft||abbr=on|sigfig=2}} altitude. It was originally discovered near the Serbian village of [[Zaovine]], on Mount [[Tara (mountain)|Tara]], in 1875, and named by the Serbian botanist [[Josif Pančić]];Farjon, A. (1990). ''Pinaceae. Drawings and Descriptions of the Genera''. Koeltz Scientific Books {{ISBN|3-87429-298-3}}.Rushforth, K. (1987). ''Conifers''. Helm {{ISBN|0-7470-2801-X}}.Rushforth, K. (1999). ''Trees of Britain and Europe''. Collins {{ISBN|0-00-220013-9}}. the [[Botanical name#Binary name|specific epithet]] {{lang|sr|omorika}} is simply the Serbian word for the tree (other spruces are {{lang|sr|smrča}} in Serbian). == Description == It is a medium-sized [[evergreen]] [[tree]] growing to {{convert|20|m|ft|0|abbr=on}} tall, exceptionally {{convert|33|m|ft|abbr=on|sigfig=2}}, with a trunk diameter of up to {{convert|0.7|m|ft|0|abbr=on}}, and a conic crown; the crown is very narrow on high altitude trees, broader at lower altitudes. The shoots are buff-brown, and densely pubescent (hairy). The [[leaf|leaves]] are needle-like, 10–20 mm long, flattened in cross-section, dark green above, and with two glaucous blue-white [[stomata|stomatal stripes]] below. The [[conifer cone|cones]] are {{convert|4|-|7|cm|0|abbr=on}} long, [[fusiform]] (spindle-shaped, broadest in the middle), dark purple (almost black) when young, maturing dark brown 5–7 months after pollination, with stiff scales. The tallest specimen in the wild currently known is 30.2 m tall;{{cite web | title=Serbian Spruces in Nacionalni park Tara in Zaovine, Šumadija and Western Serbia, Serbia | website=Monumental trees | url=https://www.monumentaltrees.com/en/srb/sumadijawesternserbia/zlatibor/22630_nacionalniparktara/ | access-date=2025-06-19}} older claims of trees up to 50 m tall are now unverifiable. In cultivation, the tallest currently known is 33 m tall, in the [[Arboretum Mustila]] in Finland,{{cite web | title=Serbian Spruce in Arboretum Mustila, Elimäki, Kymenlaakso, Finland | website=Monumental trees | date=2014-09-30 | url=https://www.monumentaltrees.com/en/fin/kymenlaakso/kouvola/9016_arboretummustila/23154/ | access-date=2025-06-19}} with another not far behind at 31.5 m at [[Murthly Castle]] in Scotland.{{cite web | title=Serbian Spruce at Murthly Castle estate, Birnam, Scotland, United Kingdom | website=Monumental trees | date=2017-06-22 | url=https://www.monumentaltrees.com/en/gbr/scotland/perthandkinross/7374_murthlycastleestate/31522/ | access-date=2025-06-19}} == Ecology == Because of its limited range, it is not a major source of nutrition to wildlife, but does provide cover for birds and small mammals. Prior to the [[Pleistocene]] [[ice ages]], it had a much larger range throughout most of [[Europe]]. File:Picea omorika, Zaovine, Serbia 5.jpg|Foliage, showing the glossy green upper side of the needles File:Picea omorika, Zaovine, Serbia 6.jpg|Foliage, showing the glaucous blue-green [[stomata|stomatal stripes]] on the underside of needles File:Picea omorika young female cone - Keila.jpg|Immature female cone File:Fichtenzapfen P4202419.jpg|Mature female cone File:PiceaOmorika30yearsFull.jpg|Although some trees are very slender, this is not invariable; many are broader, such as this cultivated tree in France File:Manabe-nouen201605-07.jpg|Cultivar 'Pendula' == Cultivation and uses == Outside its native range, Serbian spruce is of major importance as an [[ornamental tree]] in large gardens, valued in northern Europe and North America for its very attractive crown form and ability to grow on a wide range of soils, including alkaline, clay, acid and sandy soil, although it prefers moist, drained loam. The crown shape is heritable, with high altitude seed sources retaining the narrow crown in cultivation, and lower altitude sources their broader crown. It is also grown to a small extent in [[forestry]] for [[Christmas tree]]s, [[timber]] and [[paper]] production, particularly in northern Europe, though its slow growth makes it less important than [[Sitka spruce]] or [[Norway spruce]]. In cultivation, it has produced [[Hybrid (biology)|hybrids]] with the closely related [[black spruce]] (named as ''P. × mariorika''),{{cite web | title=Picea × mariorika | website=/RHS | date=2025-05-09 | url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/45102/picea-mariorika/details | access-date=2025-06-19}} and also with Sitka spruce. === AGM cultivars === The following [[cultivars]] have gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]]:{{cite web | url = https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/pdfs/agm-lists/agm-ornamentals.pdf | title = AGM Plants - Ornamental | date = July 2017 | page = 78 | publisher = Royal Horticultural Society | access-date = 25 April 2018}} * ''Picea omorika'' 'Nana'{{cite web|url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/99400/Picea-omorika-Nana/Details |title=RHS Plant Selector Picea omorika 'Nana' AGM / RHS Gardening |publisher=Apps.rhs.org.uk |date= |access-date=10 February 2021}} – a dwarf form * ''Picea omorika'' 'Pendula'{{cite web|url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/90723/Picea-omorika-Pendula/Details |title=RHS Plant Selector Picea omorika 'Pendula' AGM / RHS Gardening |publisher=Apps.rhs.org.uk |date= |access-date=10 February 2021}} – a weeping form == References == {{Reflist|2}} == External links == * {{Commons category-inline|Picea omorika|''Picea omorika''}} * ''[https://www.euforgen.org/species/picea-omorika/ Picea omorika]'' – information, genetic conservation units, and related resources.
